create.name: Kelley Weber
create.bio:
Kelley Weber is a spiritual director and contemplative teacher in St. Louis, Missouri, who works under the name A Spiral Space. She trained as an actor and director, holds an MFA, and was among the founders of Mustard Seed Theatre in the city, a company devoted to plays about faith and ethics; she has also taught for more than twenty-five years, including mindfulness in schools through Mindful Schools. She is certified in spiritual direction by the Aquinas Institute of Theology, completed the Living School at the Center for Action and Contemplation, where her teachers included Richard Rohr, James Finley and Cynthia Bourgeault, and is training in the Somatic Enneagram with Marion Gilbert.

Her own faith is grounded in the teachings of Jesus, but she writes mainly for people who feel at home in no church and still want a living inner life, and she does not try to steer anyone towards a belief. She meets directees monthly for unhurried listening and silence, offers Enneagram coaching that treats the types as a doorway to awareness in the body, and leads small contemplative day retreats near St. Louis. A free six-part course on her site, Where Has God Been All My Life?, invites readers to write a spiritual autobiography, and her short prayers and talks are on Insight Timer.

courses.title: Spiritual Direction
courses.description: Monthly one-hour meetings in which she listens closely, leaves room for silence and asks open questions, so that each person can find their own path whatever their tradition, or none. Conversations are confidential and she does not try to persuade anyone of anything.

courses.title: Enneagram Coaching
courses.description: One-to-one coaching that uses the nine Enneagram types to notice habitual patterns of avoidance and reaction, with an emphasis on awareness in the body. It is meant to sit alongside a contemplative practice, religious or secular; a free first consultation is offered.

courses.title: The Somatic Enneagram (Day Retreat)
courses.description: A Saturday day retreat, co-led with Lynda Rands at her lakeside home in Glen Carbon, Illinois, about half an hour from St. Louis. The day places Enneagram work inside mindfulness practice, learning to sense one's type's patterns in the body and steady oneself from within. Runs 10am to 3pm.

free_resources.title: Where Has God Been All My Life? A Spiritual Autobiography Course
free_resources.description: Six free lessons on her site, each with a short reflection and writing prompts, moving from presence and early images of God to the beliefs that limit us and a sense of calling. It is designed to help readers trace where the sacred has already appeared in their lives.

free_resources.title: Introduction to Mindfulness: Attention, Awareness and the Paradigm of the Seeds
free_resources.description: A plain-spoken written introduction to mindfulness that starts from everyday experiences of a wandering, looping mind and explains attention and awareness through the image of seeds we choose to water.

free_resources.title: A Practice In Contentment: Enneagram
free_resources.description: An eleven-minute guided practice on contentment framed through the Enneagram. Free on Insight Timer.

free_resources.title: The Generosity Of Silence & Listening
free_resources.description: A short guided reflection on silence and on listening as a gift to others. Free on Insight Timer.
